text:
Erik Gudbranson went third overall in 2010, one pick after Tyler Seguin, and he has spent the years since becoming one very specific kind of defenseman. Sixteen games into this season in Columbus, he has one assist, ten shots and 33 blocked shots. Nobody is asking him for offense, and our numbers agree: his individual expected goals (the quality of the chances he creates himself) add up to 0.31 for the season.

The real question is the defending. With him on the ice at five on five, the Blue Jackets have taken 43.8% of the expected goals, and Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting more chances with him on last season too (bottom 12% of defensemen). His ice time is drifting down, 12.85 minutes a night over his last ten against 14.75 for the season. There is some bad luck in his line: Columbus has scored 11.9 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him out there, and that usually swings back. For a player in his role, though, the minutes are the number to watch. They are the clearest read on how much the coaches still trust him.
headline: Erik Gudbranson's job is blocks, not points
